title: Warehouse Operations and Management
overview: Managing inventories that can total millions of dollars requires an efficient warehouse to store, maintain, and protect these valuable assets. In this course, we will explore the best and most current methods for storing and safeguarding high-value inventories, as well as the essential characteristics of a modern warehouse. Understanding what inventory you have and how much is crucial for effective warehousing management. We will delve into various techniques for achieving record accuracy and conducting successful cycle counts, utilizing a scientific approach to auditing the warehouse.
audience: This course is intended for individuals involved in warehousing operations, both at operational and supervisory levels. It is also suitable for anyone interested in learning more about the relationship between warehousing and other materials management functions.
methodology: The course employs a variety of interactive learning methods, including videos, questionnaires, case studies, team and individual exercises, as well as group discussions.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Articulate the challenges, objectives, and functions of warehousing
Conduct ABC inventory classification and cycle counting, calculating record accuracy and discrepancies
Identify different types of storage and material handling systems
Enhance supervisory skills and effectively address warehouse staff issues
Foster better housekeeping and safety practices within the warehouse
Measure warehouse productivity using appropriate Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and conduct a scientific audit of the warehouse
